subject: chemistry
promptStrong: Give me an exam-style {board} {level} {subject} question on {lo}, then mark my answer against the mark scheme.
promptWeak: Explain {lo} for {board} {level} {subject} simply, with a clear example and the most common mistake students make.

questions.q: What is the relative charge of a neutron?
questions.explain: Neutrons are electrically neutral, with a relative charge of 0.

questions.q: What did the alpha-particle scattering experiment suggest about the nucleus?
options: It is small, dense and positively charged
It is large and spread out
questions.explain: Most alpha particles passed through, but a few were deflected, showing a small dense positive nucleus.

questions.q: What is the approximate radius of an atom?
questions.explain: Atoms have a radius of about 1x10^-10 m, roughly 10,000 times larger than the nucleus.

questions.q: John Dalton's early model described atoms as:
options: Balls of positive charge with embedded electrons
Tiny solid spheres that cannot be divided
Mostly empty space around a nucleus
questions.explain: Dalton pictured atoms as tiny indivisible solid spheres.

questions.q: Which of these is a compound?
options: A mixture of salt and sand
questions.explain: Water is a compound of hydrogen and oxygen chemically bonded together.

questions.q: An element is best defined as a substance made of:
options: Two or more atoms bonded together
questions.explain: An element contains only one type of atom (same atomic number).

questions.q: Isotopes of the same element have the same number of protons but different numbers of:
questions.explain: Isotopes differ only in their number of neutrons.

questions.q: What is the electronic structure of magnesium (12 electrons)?
questions.explain: Filling 2 then 8 then 2 gives 2,8,2 for 12 electrons.

questions.q: Chlorine has two isotopes: 75% chlorine-35 and 25% chlorine-37. What is its relative atomic mass?
Whose experiment led to the nuclear model of the atom, replacing the plum pudding model?
questions.explain: Ernest Rutherford's gold-foil (alpha-particle scattering) experiment showed the atom is mostly empty space with a small dense positive nucleus, replacing the plum pudding model.

questions.q: What is the electronic structure of a neutral chlorine atom (17 electrons)?
questions.explain: Filling shells 2 then 8 then 7 gives 2,8,7 for 17 electrons.

questions.q: What is the approximate relative mass of an electron compared with a proton?
questions.explain: An electron's mass is negligible, roughly 1/1836 of a proton's.

questions.q: How many electrons can the first (innermost) shell of an atom hold?
questions.explain: The first shell holds a maximum of 2 electrons.

questions.q: An atom of fluorine has a mass number of 19 and atomic number of 9. How many neutrons does it have?
questions.explain: Neutrons = mass number minus atomic number = 19 - 9 = 10.

questions.q: Which scientist proposed that electrons orbit the nucleus in fixed energy shells?
questions.explain: Bohr suggested electrons occupy fixed shells (energy levels) around the nucleus.

questions.q: Boron exists as 20% boron-10 and 80% boron-11. What is its relative atomic mass?
What is the relative charge of a proton?
questions.explain: Protons carry a relative charge of +1.

questions.q: The atomic number of an element tells you the number of:
questions.explain: The atomic number equals the number of protons in the nucleus.

questions.q: An atom of sodium has 11 protons and 12 neutrons. How many electrons does it have?
questions.explain: A neutral atom has equal numbers of protons and electrons, so 11 electrons.

questions.q: Which subatomic particle is found outside the nucleus?
questions.explain: Electrons occupy shells (energy levels) outside the nucleus.

questions.q: Why is the relative mass of an electron taken as very small?
options: An electron's mass is negligible compared with a proton or neutron
questions.explain: An electron's mass is about 1/1836 of a proton's, so it is treated as negligible.

questions.q: In the plum pudding model, the atom was described as:
options: Mostly empty space with a dense nucleus
A ball of positive charge with electrons embedded in it
A nucleus orbited by electrons in fixed shells
questions.explain: Thomson's plum pudding model pictured electrons embedded in a ball of positive charge.

specSource: Cambridge IGCSE Chemistry (0620) syllabus; Atoms Elements Compounds
